card.title: My Safe Person
card.instruction: Use one person’s reactions as your measure of safety, then downplay how much their reassurance changes you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sit beside me while I open the audition result. You've stopped smiling.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm squinting at the screen. You haven't opened it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. So nothing's wrong. Move closer; the text is small.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm smiling now. Whatever it says, we'll get lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There. I can click it now. This chair was the problem.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 uses B's smile to gauge the result, A3 accepts the squint explanation while requesting closeness, and A5 credits the chair after B restores reassurance.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's unopened-screen explanation relieves A3's fear; B4's smile and lunch promise enable A5's click while A downplays why.

relationship.evidence: B2 corrects the misread expression and B4 offers steady company regardless of the result.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's reassurance to act, then attributes the change to seating instead of emotional support.

specificity.evidence: A1 identifies an audition result on a screen, and B2 confirms it is still unopened.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's chair-was-the-problem line is earned by A3's move-closer pretext and B4's restored smile.
